newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Bus to lift '97 deliveries 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Bus to lift '97 deliveries 15 pct.

text.p: The bus division of Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Thursday that it planned to increase deliveries in 1997 by 15 percent.

"Our goal is to increase deliveries by 15 percent this year and the two years after that. Our goal is to reach global deliveries of 20,000 buses annually," said company spokeswoman Kerstin Sterner in an interview with Reuters.
Volvo Bus plans to expand by entering new markets, making more acquisitions and starting more joint ventures, she said.
"We have 25 or so projects going around the world. We have everything to gain by entering markets we are not in today," Sterner said.
Sterner confirmed that investigations and contact-making was ongoing to set up a project in Russia, but said she was not aware of that any new steps had been taken in this area.
Volvo bus delivered around 6,800 buses in 1995. In 1996 deliveries rose to around 8,000 but the final figure will not be released until Volvo's 1996 earnings report is released on February 19.
